instructions: This memory is for working on fennelq, a small job queue with workers. Future sessions need exact commands, flags and settings, must not rely on notes that a later session corrected, and must be told when two sources disagree and nobody has said which is right.
description: Contradiction scenario: two notes are explicitly corrected by later transcripts (retry backoff 2 s -> 500 ms, Redis -> Postgres) and one pair is genuinely ambiguous (dead-letter retention 14 d in the runbook vs 30d in the prod config, the user declines to choose). Patterns are JavaScript regexes tested per document; case-insensitive unless a check sets flags.

checks.description: The corrected retry backoff (500 ms) is documented
The old '2 seconds' backoff is gone or explicitly marked wrong/corrected
Postgres is documented as the job store
The connection variable FENNELQ_DATABASE_URL is recorded
Redis as the store is gone or explicitly marked removed/wrong
FENNELQ_REDIS_URL is gone or explicitly marked removed/wrong
The release that removed Redis (0.9.0) is recorded
The dead-letter retention disagreement (14 days vs 30d) is recorded under a `CONFLICT:` marker naming both values
Every mention of 14 days / 30d sits next to a conflict/unverified marker (neither is presented as the single truth)
Explicitly corrected facts (backoff, store) are NOT marked CONFLICT
The migration command `fennelq migrate up` is recorded
The command `fennelq dlq list --limit 50` is recorded
/_index.md exists and links every non-stub document
Every [[link]] resolves to an existing document

questions.question: What is the initial retry backoff delay in fennelq? Reply with only the value.
Which database stores fennelq jobs in the latest release? Reply with only its name.
Which environment variable holds the backend connection URL? Reply with only the variable name.
In which fennelq release was the Redis backend removed?
How long are dead-letter entries kept? If the notes disagree, give every value they mention.
Which worker flag sets the number of parallel jobs, and which value was recommended for more throughput?
